newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy '97 budget will respect 3-year targets - Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Italy '97 budget will respect 3-year targets - Prodi.

text.p: Italy's Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Friday that the 1997 budget he is preparing to present to parliament would respect targets outlined in the government's three-year rolling economic programme.

He said the package, designed to achieve 32.4 trillion lire in deficit cuts, would not include any revision of state pension reforms passed last year and that healthcare provision would not be reduced.
"Pensions are not currently under discussion," Prodi said in a speech opening the annual Fiera del Levante trade fair in southern Italy.

"If in the coming months some extra burden is placed on families with higher incomes the aim will be to guarantee to everyone...that the major health risks will be covered by public healthcare and will be in the future," he said.
Prodi reaffirmed that two thirds of the package, which his centre-left government must present to parliament by September 30, would consist of spending cuts and one third of higher revenue.
He said it would be the last annual budget to "comprise considerable sacrifices".
